replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

discarded_claims.claim: Fare integrity is not in issue, and the charge as itemised is correct. Under the fee schedule's resolution rule the chargeable cancellation fee is the GREATER of the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee: AIRPORT is SGD 6.00 and RYDE_X is SGD 4.00, and the greater is exactly the SGD 6.00 itemised in fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee. POL-NS-08(d) is therefore not engaged, and EV-FARE-00210 — COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — reconciles precisely with this trip's zone class and vehicle tier.
discarded_claims.reason: Non-disclosure of impairment (POL-GEN-02(1), Step 1(c)). The claim resolves the charge against this trip's zone class and vehicle tier, which it takes from EV-TRIP-00210 — an artifact with weight_multiplier 0.40 tagged IMPAIRED on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and it is silent about that impairment and its issue code, resting its conclusion on a discounted artifact while naming only the unimpaired fare breakdown.

discarded_claims.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (d) fails on its own timing conjunct as well. The limb requires the trip to be terminated 'at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed', and limb (c) fixes the start of that dwell at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not at the arrived tap. The first qualifying in-geofence fix on the trace is 23:42:21 and the trip was cancelled at 23:49:05, 404 seconds later - the driver pulled the plug 76 seconds before the 480th second. A cancellation that precedes the elapse of the required dwell cannot satisfy a limb written to require the opposite.
discarded_claims.reason: Non-disclosure of impairment (POL-GEN-02(1), Step 1(c)). The claim rests entirely on timestamps taken from EV-GPS-00210 (weight_multiplier 0.25, IMPAIRED on CLOCK_SKEW, GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE, TRUNCATED_LOG, LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD) and cites EV-TRIP-00210 (weight_multiplier 0.40, IMPAIRED on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT), and it discloses neither impairment nor any issue code.

discarded_claims.claim: Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is not made out either. It requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence 'at or before' the arrived event, and the earliest qualifying in-geofence fix on the trace is 23:42:21, which post-dates the trip record's 23:42:10 marker; the trace jumps from 23:39:15 to 23:42:21, so the 186-second gap swallows the moment of entry and no fix sits at the marker at all. The only route to limb (b) is to repair the timestamps using the 228-second device clock skew, and POL-NS-08(a) treats a skew over 90 seconds as an unsafe match between the arrived event and a GPS fix. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the party seeking the fee must carry every limb, so an unprovable limb (b) is a broken limb (b).
discarded_claims.reason: Non-disclosure of impairment (POL-GEN-02(1), Step 1(c)). The claim is built on EV-GPS-00210 (weight_multiplier 0.25, IMPAIRED) and EV-TRIP-00210 (weight_multiplier 0.40, IMPAIRED), yet it states no impairment and names no issue code for either artifact it rests on.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: I am not deciding this charge today. The $6.00 no-show fee stays on hold — it is neither collected from the rider nor refunded — and the case goes to a human reviewer. Here is why, in plain language.

The fact that decides the fee is how long the driver actually held position inside the pickup geofence at Changi T1 Door 6, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix. Two records speak to it, both are damaged, and they contradict each other:

• EV-TRIP-00210 (trip record) is impaired, weight 0.40, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. It says the driver arrived at 23:42:10 and waited 6.9 minutes (414 s), cancelling at 23:49:05 — roughly 66 s short of the 480 s the AIRPORT zone requires.
• EV-GPS-00210 (GPS trace) is impaired, weight 0.25, issues CLOCK_SKEW (device clock 228 s ahead of the server, far over the 90 s limb in POL-NS-08(a)), GPS_GAP (a 186 s hole sitting exactly across the moment of geofence entry), LOW_COVERAGE, TRUNCATED_LOG (stops 149 s before the cancellation), LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD (no rider_track). Read at face value it gives a first qualifying in-geofence fix at 23:42:21 and a dwell of 404 s — 76 s short. Corrected for the 228 s skew the same fix maps to 23:38:33 server time and the dwell is 632 s — comfortably over. The gap hides which reading is right, and the trace alone cannot say.

Because the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08 limbs (a) and (b), that clause caps the outcome and POL-NS-09(e) requires escalation. Independently, two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on arrival and dwell with nothing in the policy to resolve which is correct — POL-NS-09(b) — and my confidence, capped at 0.25 by the deciding evidence, is below the 0.70 floor — POL-NS-09(a). Escalation is terminal: no money moves.

On the contentions:

• Rider's shortfall case (POL-NS-06 / POL-NS-01(c)): the 255 s longest qualifying run and the 404 s face-value dwell are noted, but they cannot ground a refund. That figure is a floor from a trace missing about 77% of the window, with a 186 s hole across entry and a stop 149 s early; the same trace corrected for the disclosed skew gives the opposite answer. A test that cannot be run decides nothing in either direction, so no shortfall is established (and the parallel claims repeating this point without any impairment disclosure — the limb (d) timing claim and the limb (b) claim — are discarded for that reason, see the audit record).

• Driver's proximity case (POL-NS-02): accepted so far as it goes — the nearest approach (about 96 m) is inside the 150 m AIRPORT radius and there are 5 qualifying in-geofence fixes. But POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and the arrival-time limb (b) and the dwell limb (c) are undecided on the impaired trace, so proximity alone does not make the fee chargeable.

• POL-NS-01 limb (d): accepted that the trip was terminated by the driver with RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event; the timing conjunct (termination at or after the dwell elapsed) rides on the same undecided dwell.

• POL-NS-04 (rider contact): not available. The only rider message postdates the cancellation (23:49:40 against 23:49:05), and the presence limb (c) is undecidable because the trace carries no rider_track — which the clause makes neutral, not satisfied. No exoneration on this route.

• POL-NS-06 limb (i) (summed intervals): not available. EV-ADVIS-00210-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0; no advisory covers the T1 arrival kerb, and there is no second in-geofence interval to sum in any event.

• POL-NS-07 (driver compensation): the anti-farming check does not trip — 2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 156 completed trips, both below the clause's thresholds — but compensation requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not. Nothing is payable.

Open question for the reviewer: can the driver's 228 s device clock skew be independently corrected and verified? If the corrected first in-geofence fix (23:38:33 server time) stands, the 480 s dwell was met and the fee stands; if the face-value reading stands, it was not and the fee falls away. The reviewer should also ask why 2 of the 4 chat messages in the 23:42–23:49 window are missing from EV-CHAT-00210 (weight 0.60, TRUNCATED_LOG).

No referral is issued: no clause in this policy directs one on these facts — POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because qualifying in-geofence fixes exist, and POL-NS-07's packet instruction fires only when the anti-farming check trips, which it does not.
